questions.text: A SaaS company adds rate limits and CAPTCHAs specifically to stop customers from scraping their own data out of the product.
questions.detail: The product has no export feature. The terms of service say customers own their data.

questions.text: Your team ships a feature that doesn't work with screen readers to hit a launch date, planning to fix it next quarter.
Your company trains an AI model on customer support transcripts. The privacy policy permits it, but customers were never told directly.
Product asks you to make cancelling a subscription require a phone call, while signing up takes one click.
You find a security vulnerability in last year's release. It's patched, there's no evidence it was exploited, and leadership decides not to tell customers.
You ship code written by an AI assistant that passes every test, but you don't fully understand how it works.
